sentences.text: Slow English Podcast with your host, Emilie, episode talking about Germany.
Today, we will talk about Germany. Germany is a big and important country in Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and simple English. You can listen and repeat if you want.
Let's begin. Where is Germany? Germany is in Central Europe.
It shares borders with many countries. It is next to France, Poland, Austria, Switzerland,
the Netherlands, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark and Luxembourg. Germany has both mountains and seas.
To the north, it has the north sea and the Baltic sea. To the south, there are the Alps,
big snowy mountains. What is the capital city of Germany? The capital city is Berlin.
Berlin is a big and modern city. It has history, art and music.
It is also green with many parks and lakes. Berlin was once divided into two parts,
East Berlin and West Berlin. Now it is one city again. You can still see the Berlin Wall,
a symbol of history. Other large cities in Germany are Hamburg, Munich, Cologne,
Frankfurt and Stuttgart. How many people live in Germany? About 84 million people live in Germany.
It is the most populated country in the European Union. Many people live in cities,
but there are also small towns and villages. Germany is a mix of old and new,
history and technology together. What language do people speak in Germany? People speak German.
German is the official language. It is spoken in schools, on the radio and at work.
Many people in Germany also speak English, especially young people.
In schools, children learn English from an early age. In some regions, people also speak regional
dialects or minority languages, like Turkish, Arabic or Polish. What is the weather like in Germany?
Germany has four seasons. Spring, summer, autumn and winter. Spring is green and fresh. Flowers
bloom and people enjoy walks. Summer is warm, but not too hot. It is a good time for swimming,
cycling and traveling. Autumn is cool with colorful leaves. People harvest apples and grapes.
Winter is cold. It often snows in the south. People wear warm coats and drink hot tea.
What does Germany look like? Germany has many different landscapes. Mountains in the south,
flat plains in the north, rivers like the Rhine, Danube and Elbe. Forests like the Black Forest,
castles on hills, lakes and vineyards. Germany is also famous for its beautiful villages,
with timber houses and flowers in the windows. What animals live in Germany? Germany has many
animals in the wild and on farms. In forests, you can see deer, foxes, wild boars and hairs.
In the Alps, you can see ibex and eagles. On farms, there are cows, pigs, chickens and sheep.
Germany also has zoos, animal parks and nature reserves to protect animals.
What do people eat in Germany? German food is warm and filling. People eat bread,
meat, potatoes and vegetables. Some popular foods are
bratwurst, grilled sausage, sauerkraut, sour cabbage, schnitzel, fried meat cutlet,
pretzel, soft bread twist, potato salad, rye bread with cheese or ham. In the south,
people eat spezel, a kind of pasta. In the north, people eat more fish. For dessert,
they enjoy apple cake, apple kuken, black forest cake and chocolate. What do people drink in Germany?
Germany is famous for beer. There are many types of beer in different regions,
but people also drink water, juice, tea and coffee. Children often drink apple juice or fizzy water.
What is life like in Germany? Life in Germany is organized and balanced. People go to school,
work and enjoy their weekends. Germany has a strong education system. Children go to school,
Monday to Friday. Many schools finish around lunchtime. People like to go for walks in nature,
ride bicycles, visit family, go to concerts or museums, watch football, soccer.
Sundays are quiet, shops are closed and people rest. What are some German traditions and holidays?
October Fest, a big beer and music festival in Munich. Christmas markets with lights,
food and gifts in December. Easter with chocolate eggs and spring flowers. Carnival colorful costumes
and parades, especially in Cologne. Tagtor Deutsch in Einheit. Day of Unity. Celebrated on October 3rd.
Some fun facts about Germany. Germany has more than 20,000 castles. The Autobahn is a fast highway
with no speed limit in some places. Germany is the home of famous thinkers like Albert Einstein
and Beethoven. Germany is known for cars like Volkswagen, BMW and Mercedes Benz. The German flag
is black, red and gold. Now you know many things about Germany. You know where it is,
what people speak and how they live. You learned about the weather, food, animals and holidays.
Goodbye. Or as they say in German. Chews.
